title: The Last Debt
premise: Dominic Iversen, a private security contractor haunted by a botched protection detail that killed his client, takes one last low-profile job guarding a courier named Mara Voss. Mid-flight, every record of the aircraft vanishes from radar, manifests, and databases, and the plane lands at a decommissioned airfield where armed men await a passenger who officially never existed. Dominic realizes the flight carried evidence implicating Halcyon Group, the security conglomerate that trained him, and that the 'incident' that broke him was engineered to bury the same secret. Hunted across two days by his own former colleagues, Dominic must choose between selling out Mara to buy his way back into invisibility or exposing Halcyon and finally facing what he did. At dawn, as the extraction flight idles on the runway, he trades the secret not for escape but for testimony, boarding the plane as a witness rather than a fugitive.
about_author: Gideon Vasquez is a former maritime insurance investigator who spent a decade documenting how paper trails disappear. He writes thrillers about ordinary professionals trapped inside systems designed to forget them.

chapters.title: Nights Without Floors
chapters.summary: Dominic's POV. Insomnia-ridden Dominic works a dead-end corporate guard job in Lisbon, flinching at doorways and replaying the incident in Prague. A fixer offers him a simple escort gig: meet a courier at the airport, fly her to Casablanca, hand her off. He accepts because invisible work is all he can bear. Beat: numbness mistaken for peace.

chapters.title: The Woman With Two Names
chapters.summary: Mara's POV. Mara Voss checks into the airport hotel under a false name, carrying a sealed case she was told never to open. She clocks Dominic instantly as ex-military muscle and tests him with small lies. She trusts no one, least of whoever hired her. Beat: wary competence masking fear.

chapters.title: Boarding Pass to Nowhere
chapters.summary: Dominic's POV. The charter is clean, the crew professional, but Dominic notices the flight plan filed under a shell company he recognizes from his Halcyon days. Mara boards with the case chained to her wrist. As they climb over the Atlantic, he decides it's coincidence. Beat: dread deferred.

chapters.title: Vanishing Point
chapters.summary: Multiple POV. Ninety minutes out, the plane blinks off radar; the pilot's transponder code returns 'not found.' The co-pilot's tablet shows their manifest deleted mid-sentence. The captain turns back toward an unlisted strip in southern Portugal. Beat: the world quietly erasing them.

chapters.title: Ground That Isn't on Maps
chapters.summary: Dominic's POV. They land at a derelict NATO field where floodlights snap on before the engines stop. Men in unmarked gear surround the plane asking for 'the asset.' Dominic lies smoothly, buying minutes, while Mara slips the case into a maintenance crawlspace. Beat: instinct outrunning thought.

chapters.title: What Halcyon Builds
chapters.summary: Dominic's POV, flashback-woven. Held in a hangar office, Dominic recognizes the operation's signature: Halcyon's asset-recovery protocol, the same machinery that manufactured the Prague incident. He realizes his past wasn't failure—it was rehearsal. Beat: the floor of his self-narrative giving way.

chapters.title: The Case
chapters.summary: Mara's POV. Interrogated separately, Mara bargains with half-truths while recalling her handler's last instruction: if anyone from Halcyon appears, the case goes public. Alone in her cell, she retrieves a hidden backup drive from her jacket lining. Beat: fear sharpening into resolve.

chapters.title: Old Colleagues
chapters.summary: Anton Reyes' POV. Halcyon recovery lead Anton Reyes arrives by helicopter, delighted to find Dominic among the detainees—an old protégé gone soft. He offers Dominic reinstatement: deliver Mara and the case, and Prague gets reclassified as enemy action. Beat: temptation wearing a friendly face.

chapters.title: Price List
chapters.summary: Dominic's POV. Alone, Dominic weighs the offer: his record scrubbed, his nights quiet again, in exchange for a woman who trusted him for eleven hours. He asks for time. Reyes grants it, because Reyes already knows what Dominic will choose—or believes he does. Beat: shame doing arithmetic.

chapters.title: Crawlspace Gospel
chapters.summary: Mara's POV. Mara escapes her cell through a ventilation duct during a generator test and reaches the crawlspace—only to find the case moved. She finds Dominic waiting there instead, having tracked the guards' rotation. Guns drawn, neither shoots. Beat: two liars recognizing each other.

chapters.title: Terms of Survival
chapters.summary: Dual POV. In the dark of the hangar, Mara shows Dominic fragments: Halcyon sold targeting data that got civilians killed, and Prague was cleanup. Dominic tells her the truth about Prague—that he froze, and his client died. An ugly, necessary honesty. They form a pact. Beat: belonging forged from confession.

chapters.title: The Long Corridor
chapters.summary: Dominic's POV. Moving through the base's service tunnels, they trigger a lockdown. Dominic uses Halcyon protocols against Halcyon men, and hates how well his body remembers. Mara watches him become the thing he despises to keep them alive. Beat: survival costing pieces of the soul.

chapters.title: Signal Fire
chapters.summary: Mara's POV. From the control tower, Mara broadcasts the case's index on an open aviation frequency—a dead man's switch that starts a clock. Somewhere, journalists and regulators begin receiving fragments. Reyes hears the transmission and stops negotiating. Beat: the secret turning into a weapon.

chapters.title: Hunted on the Tarmac
chapters.summary: Dominic's POV. A running battle across fuel depots as dawn approaches. Dominic takes a graze covering Mara's sprint to the extraction charter—the same flight model as theirs, prepped for Reyes's own exit. He realizes the extraction flight is real, fueled, and leaving at first light. Beat: adrenaline with grief underneath.

chapters.title: Reyes's Offer, Final Draft
chapters.summary: Anton's POV. Cornering Mara at gunpoint, Reyes makes his pitch one last time—not to her, but through her, knowing Dominic listens on her open mic. Full amnesty, money, erasure. All Dominic must do is walk away and let Reyes put a bullet in the problem. Beat: the devil quoting scripture.

chapters.title: The One Secret Worth Killing For
chapters.summary: Dominic's POV. Dominic steps into the floodlights and gives Reyes what he asked for: the case's location. But the location is a decoy—and the real trade Dominic offers is himself, his sworn testimony, in exchange for Mara walking onto that extraction flight alive. Beat: sacrifice disguised as surrender.

chapters.title: Dawn Extraction
chapters.summary: Dual POV. Engines spooling, Mara refuses to board without him; Dominic forces the choice on her with a lie about following on the next plane. Reyes's men drag Dominic back as the charter lifts off. Mara, airborne, opens the case and begins transmitting everything. Beat: heartbreak weaponized.

chapters.title: Interrogation at First Light
chapters.summary: Dominic's POV. In the hangar, Reyes can't kill him yet—the broadcast has made Dominic valuable as the man who can confirm everything. Dominic stalls, bleeds, and talks: not confessions, but coordinates, names, dates, each fact a hook for the incoming storm. Beat: endurance as defiance.

chapters.title: Everything Lands
chapters.summary: Multiple POV. Within hours, regulators freeze Halcyon assets; a prosecutor's warrant names Reyes. The base floods with police and press. Reyes, cornered, chooses violence over arrest, and Dominic—exhausted, half-broken—chooses not to look away this time. Beat: recklessness transmuted into courage.

chapters.title: The Incident, Retold
chapters.summary: Dominic's POV. In a prosecutor's office, Dominic gives his full account of Prague, including his own failure, on the record. The words cost more than any bullet. For the first time since, he describes the incident without flinching. Beat: grief given a legal shape, then released.

chapters.title: Belonging
chapters.summary: Mara's POV. Weeks later, Mara finds Dominic working honest, unglamorous security at a coastal port. She brings coffee and the news that the case broke open a parliamentary inquiry. Neither says thank you; both stay past sunset. Beat: cautious warmth between survivors.

chapters.title: First Sleep
chapters.summary: Dominic's POV. Dominic falls asleep in a chair by an open window, sea air moving through the room, no dreams of Prague waiting. He wakes at dawn naturally, rested, and doesn't reach for the phone. The debt isn't paid—but it's finally his to carry, not to flee. Beat: quiet, earned peace.
